extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators; administrators, legal counsel, and policymakers at recipients of Federal education funds (IHEs, LEAs, other recipients); stakeholders who implement or evaluate Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and Regulatory Impact Analysis accompanying the Department's Title IX final rule describing regulatory requirements, compliance expectations, and estimated costs and benefits for recipients (IHEs, LEAs, and other entities receiving Federal education funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirement (final §106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.8(f) broadens recordkeeping requirements to apply to all notifications to the Title IX Coordinator about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and all complaints of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes recipients may need to modify existing systems; many recipients already maintain records under state/local law or the 2020 amendments. For recipients that only tracked sexual harassment previously, burden increases with volume of records for other forms of sex discrimination. Time estimates: LEA modifications — 2 hours each from Title IX Coordinator and administrative assistant; IHE modifications — 4 hours Title IX Coordinator, 8 hours administrative assistant, 4 hours database administrator ($77.54/hour); other recipients — 2 hours each Title IX Coordinator and administrative assistant. Estimated Year 1 cost ~ $13,022,034; ongoing annual increase ~ $5,237,728. Department received no supplementary data to alter estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and maintenance of documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must create and maintain documentation related to notifications, complaints, informal resolutions, investigations, and other Title IX processes as required by the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIA categorizes creation and maintenance of documentation as a cost category (estimated amounts provided in accounting table). Department notes many recipients already have systems that may meet requirements; others will incur costs to modify or develop recordkeeping and documentation practices. Documentation obligations are intertwined with §106.8 and other procedural provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor the recipient's program/activity for barriers to reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must ensure its Title IX Coordinator monitors the education program or activity for barriers to reporting conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and take steps reasonably calculated to address such barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many recipients (especially IHEs) may already monitor for barriers. Low-cost options include incorporating reporting-barrier questions into existing trainings, conversations with stakeholders, roundtables, or listening sessions. Remedial steps are often de minimis (e.g., remind stakeholders about reporting options during trainings, report employees discouraging reporting to HR). The Department recognizes a wide range of potential responses with varying costs and benefits and lacked supplementary data to refine estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation space availability for students and employees (final §106.40(b)(3)(v) and §106.57(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure that students and employees can access a lactation space (not a bathroom) that is clean, shielded from view, free from intrusion, and may be used for expressing breast milk or breastfeeding as needed; employees must also receive reasonable break time to express breast milk or breastfeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements align closely with FLSA and various state laws. Department anticipates de minimis costs because many employers already provide such spaces or can repurpose existing spaces; no specific size or feature requirements beyond privacy and cleanliness; temporary or converted spaces sufficient if available when needed. Systems to administer use (e.g., sign-up) can be adapted. Department expects potential retention benefits for students and employees; lacked data to quantify demand changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable break time for employee lactation (final §106.57(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide reasonable break time for an employee to express breast milk or breastfeed as needed, and ensure access to a lactation space (clean, non-bathroom, private).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department anticipates most employers already cover this for employees under FLSA; reasonable break time can be managed via existing coverage systems (e.g., for LEA teachers who need coverage). Costs likely minimal; may vary with demand and local scheduling constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications for students because of pregnancy or related conditions (final §106.40(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make reasonable modifications for a student's pregnancy or related conditions as defined in final §106.2, building on prior obligations to ensure access to educational programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies and codifies earlier OCR guidance (2013 Pregnancy Pamphlet). Examples of reasonable modifications include providing a larger desk, permitting frequent bathroom trips, or temporary elevator access. Department expects these requirements to be similar in cost to prior obligations and not to be significantly more costly; no supplementary data to change estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation consistent with gender identity (final §106.31(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: In circumstances where different treatment or separation on the basis of sex is permitted, a recipient must not carry out such treatment in a way that discriminates based on sex by subjecting a person to more than de minimis harm; adopting policies/practices that prevent participation consistent with gender identity causes more than de minimis harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May require updating policies or training materials but should not require significant expenditures (e.g., construction). Many schools already permit participation consistent with gender identity and may need no changes. Costs for investigations or training related to this provision are addressed elsewhere in the RIA; potential litigation costs acknowledged. Department ties this clarification to case law protecting against discrimination based on sex stereotypes and gender identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify the scope of Title IX protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations specify that Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination includes discrimination on the basis of pregnancy or related conditions, sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department acknowledges clarifying scope could increase costs for recipients that had not previously addressed these bases, but finds the non-monetary benefits of clarity and broader protections justify implementation costs. This clarification is intended to ensure recipients understand obligations across these forms of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify geographic scope to include off-campus conduct under certain circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Department considered and in the final regulations includes instances of off-campus conduct within Title IX's scope when such conduct affects the recipient's education program or activity (including conduct subject to a recipient's disciplinary authority or that contributes to a sex-based hostile environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department recognizes potential increased costs for recipients in addressing off-campus conduct, but expects many already address such conduct through alternative disciplinary proceedings prior to the 2020 amendments. Department argues benefits of addressing off-campus conduct (reducing profound and long-lasting impacts) justify associated costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply regulatory grievance procedure requirements to all sex discrimination complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations apply grievance procedure requirements beyond certain forms of sexual harassment to other forms of sex discrimination—closing a gap where grievance obligations previously attached only to specified sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department found the 2020 amendments may have created a gap that left recipients with no obligation to act if no formal complaint filed; extending grievance procedures ensures prompt and effective action, safeguards fairness, requires supportive measures/remedies, and improves enforcement. Costs of updating the nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures are captured in the RIA's policy revision and training cost categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow adaptation by educational level (distinguish between LEAs and IHEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Department considered but did not adopt a uniform, identical approach preventing recipients from tailoring procedures by educational level; final regulations enable recipients to adapt fair grievance procedures responsive to their educational environment (e.g., LEA operational realities vs IHEs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department notes potential unquantified benefits from enabling recipients to adapt procedures to context; acknowledges it cannot fully quantify benefits or costs of this flexibility but indicates failure to allow adaptation would impede Title IX's objectives. Stakeholder concerns from LEAs influenced this consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supportive measures and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide appropriate supportive measures to complainants and respondents and remedies to complainants or any person the recipient identifies as having their equal access limited or denied by sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are listed as a cost category in the accounting table (estimated amounts). Department views these as essential for safeguarding fairness in grievance procedures and ensuring access; costs are treated in the RIA under supportive measures and related training/updating categories.
